items.snippet: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.

items.title: Democrats win House by largest margin in 50 years. And, COP31 ends with no deal
items.snippet: Democrats have currently flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. And, climate change talks at COP31 ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history.

items.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
items.snippet: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.

items.title: Ukraine war spilling into NATO territory
items.snippet: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.

items.title: Luxury development planned on land some Albanians say is theirs, not Jared Kushner's
items.snippet: A company working for President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner purchased 300 acres of Albanian land for more than $130 million in April. But Albanians in the area tell NPR this is not Kushner's land -- it's theirs.

items.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
items.snippet: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

items.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
items.snippet: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming.

items.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
items.snippet: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

items.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
items.snippet: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

items.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
items.snippet: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.

items.title: Pneumonia complicates Jair Bolsonaro's hospital stay in Brasília
items.snippet: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been diagnosed with pneumonia at the Brasília hospital where he has been admitted since Friday with an intestinal obstruction, his doctors said on Monday, although they ruled out surgery after his intestinal condition improved.

items.title: UK expresses support for Pedro Alliana's government in Paraguay
items.snippet: The United Kingdom has expressed its support for the government of Paraguayan President Pedro Alliana, who took office just over two weeks ago after the removal of Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, Paraguay's Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after assurances from the US government
items.snippet: Nvidia's board on Monday reinstated founder Jensen Huang as chief executive and board member, weeks after his resignation, after receiving information from senior US government officials indicating that his return poses no risk to national security.

items.title: Bolsonaro "clinically stable" in intensive care with an intestinal obstruction
items.snippet: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, in intensive care with an intestinal obstruction, is "clinically stable", the DF Star hospital in Brasília said on Sunday. Bolsonaro, 71, is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup, under house arrest.

items.snippet: The government of Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella asked the social network X on Sunday to suspend the account of former President Gustavo Petro, after he called on the public to demand the president's resignation.
